clue.text: Sport I have first gathering in mushrooms

parts.note: sport in the sense of amusement or play means fun

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word gathering

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone playing a game goes out gathering mushrooms in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have first' means I has G, the first letter of 'gathering', in front of it, giving GI after FUN; 'in' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are the most familiar members of the fungus kingdom, which takes this Latin plural.

clue.text: Top man in building industry sounds an abusive type

definitions.meaning: a roofer who lays slates works at the very top of a building
to slate is to criticise harshly, so one who does so is abusive

explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is only a link here: the one word carries both senses, the second built from the verb slate, meaning to attack in words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who covers roofs with slates, and also someone who slates, or savagely criticises, others.

clue.text: Stendhal's hiding place

indicators.note: a hiding is a thrashing, so the novelist's name is beaten into a new order

parts.note: the French novelist's name, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: The French novelist Stendhal had a secret refuge somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' pretends to mean concealment but is a beating, the anagram signal; the Shetland Islands lie north of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetland is a group of Scottish islands, a geographical location.

clue.text: They're outstanding on land and sea, so one girl finds

definitions.text: They're outstanding on land and sea

indicators.note: finds suggests the letters are come upon in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl discovers striking structures standing out both ashore and offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: SO, I (one) and GIRL are rearranged; 'outstanding' means standing up out of the ground or water, as drilling towers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilling platforms for petroleum tower above the landscape or the waves.

clue.text: Aquatic creature softly goes into ground

indicators.note: the musical letter for softly is placed inside the word for ground

parts.note: ground or land is terrain
P, piano, is the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: A water animal quietly burrows into the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, an animal living in water.

clue.text: Obsession about domestic animals?

parts.note: an idea one keeps returning to is a pet idea, and the question mark invites reading pet literally as household animals

explanation.walkthrough: The grid as held reads SET THEORY, but only a 'pet' theory is an obsession, and pets are domestic animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite idea or hobby-horse that someone keeps pressing is called a pet idea of theirs.

clue.text: It doesn't come straight from one's head

definitions.text: It doesn't come straight from one's head

parts.words: It doesn't come straight from one's head
parts.note: sounds like an idea that is not original, but describes locks that are not straight growing from the scalp

explanation.definitionFit: Ringlets or waves are locks that grow in coils rather than straight down.

clue.text: Left flat by the Scottish loch

parts.note: flat or level means even

explanation.surface: Someone was abandoned in a flat beside a Highland lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like abandoned and 'flat' like an apartment; 'by' only links. Loch Leven is a lake in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Leven is a well-known lake in Kinross, Scotland.

clue.text: Audible lot of cattle!

definitions.meaning: audible things are heard, a word said exactly like the answer, so this is a definition by sound
a group of cows grazing or driven together

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works by sound only: 'Audible' means heard, which is pronounced the same as the answer; the exclamation mark flags the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove of cows is this group noun, and its sound-alike means perceived by the ear.

clue.text: He sports a riot tag

indicators.note: sports here means displays a version of, so the letters show off a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man wears a label saying riot, as a troublemaker might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' looks like wears, but signals rearranging A RIOT TAG; 'He' is the definition, a man who stirs things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser who stirs people to protest is a man of this kind.

clue.text: Mistakes one makes in Latin

definitions.meaning: errors or slips in a printed text
the Latin plural for the slips a person commits

explanation.definitionFit: Errata is a list of printing errors, and is literally the Latin word for errors.

clue.text: For a Malay sailing boat

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A request on behalf of a sailing vessel from Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a fast outrigger vessel from the Malay archipelago.

clue.text: A divinely expressed wish

parts.note: a farewell blessing calling on the Almighty to grant someone success on a journey

explanation.definitionFit: Wishing someone a safe and prosperous journey invokes heavenly favour.

clue.text: Resolve to discourage an explosive device

parts.note: to discourage is to deter
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: A determination to put people off with a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve a question is to settle or decide it.

clue.text: Observes Marxists swallowing fish

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for communists takes the fish inside it

parts.note: communists are informally called Reds
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Someone watches left-wing revolutionaries eating fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it or watch it closely.

clue.text: Means by which Scotland Yard discover gold?

definitions.text: Means by which Scotland Yard discover gold?

parts.words: Means by which Scotland Yard discover gold?
parts.note: detectives (Scotland Yard's CID) might run a test, and gold is traditionally proved by nitric acid

explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters; its detective branch is the CID, which sits inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold resists nitric acid, so a decisive trial of worth is named after the assay.

clue.text: Backdrop to the situation at railway termini

parts.note: the situation or setting is the scene

indicators.note: termini are the ends of a line, so take the first and last letters of railway

explanation.surface: A backdrop to the situation at a station where trains end their journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'termini' looks like railway stations but asks for the first and last letters of 'railway'; 'to' and 'at' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted scenery forms the background behind actors on stage.

clue.text: Flower a two-wheeler man replanted

indicators.note: replanted means the letters are set out again in new positions, apt for a flower

parts.note: a two-wheeler is a bicycle, or cycle

explanation.surface: A man on a bicycle puts a flower back in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a plant with upswept pink or white blooms.

clue.text: He gets French wine at a mini malcharge

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
the smallest charge, a cent being a tiny coin

explanation.surface: A man buys French wine at the lowest possible price.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held runs 'minimal' together wrongly as 'mini malcharge'; read it as 'a minimal charge'. 'gets' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent is a male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: An illness due to fruit repeating, it's said

indicators.note: repeating means the fruit word is given twice over
it's said tells us the word is spoken, not written

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill from eating fruit that keeps coming back on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeating' looks like indigestion but doubles the fruit; 'it's said' turns BERRY into the sound-alike BERI, giving the disease's name twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by deficiency of thiamine, vitamin B1.

clue.text: Right to look around a S. Australian Lake

indicators.note: around means the word for look goes about the abbreviation for right

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to explore a lake in South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Eyre is the large salt lake in South Australia.

clue.text: Popular craze starting about last month

parts.note: C, circa, is the abbreviation for about
ult., ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A fashionable fad began around the end of last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' places C first; 'ult' is old commercial shorthand, 'yours of the 5th ult.' meaning last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult following is a fashionable enthusiasm among a devoted group.

clue.text: Devastating winger

parts.note: sounds like a destructive footballer on the wing, but is an insect that strips crops in swarms

explanation.definitionFit: Swarming grasshoppers of this kind fly in and destroy whole harvests.

clue.text: Apprehend a musical round

definitions.meaning: to apprehend is to seize or arrest
a comic round for several voices, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries

explanation.definitionFit: To seize a suspect, and also a humorous canon sung by successive voices.

clue.text: Merits a change for one who makes a big hit

definitions.text: one who makes a big hit

indicators.note: a change of the letters means they are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone who achieves a huge success deserves a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a big hit' suggests a success; here it means one who strikes hard. 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strikes another forcefully deals a heavy blow.

clue.text: Cleaner fuel, apparently

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a domestic cleaner
coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: A fuel that burns more cleanly than others, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like an adjective, cleaner-burning, but is a British word for a cleaning woman; 'apparently' admits the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is burnt wood, a fuel that gives off little smoke.

clue.text: Aromatic plant found in sea-wreck

indicators.note: to wreck is to destroy, so the letters before it are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A scented herb washed up among ocean debris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-wreck' looks like a single noun for flotsam, but 'wreck' is the anagram signal acting on IN SEA; 'found' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is a Mediterranean herb whose seeds taste of liquorice.

clue.text: Divide into parts and bury the body

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a sect is a body of followers

explanation.surface: Cut a corpse up and bury it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' suggests a corpse but means a group of people; 'and' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cut across, dividing a space into pieces.
